newsitem.title: CANADA: StatsCan stocks report bullish for oilseeds--trade.
newsitem.headline: StatsCan stocks report bullish for oilseeds--trade.

text.p: Canola and flax cash and futures prices should get a boost from Tuesday morning's Statistics Canada stocks report for the end of the 1995/96 (Aug/July) crop year, agricultural analysts told Reuters.
"The oilseed side seems very bullish," United Grain Growers analyst Mike Jubinville said.
Total canola stocks on July 31, 1995, were pegged at 901,000 tonnes, below trade expectations.
"That lower (canola) carry-in with the weather and disease gives more underlying support," Bank of Nova Scotia unit Scotia McLeod analyst Rob Gigiel said.
"It shows higher domestic usage, that's 200,000 tonnes less than I thought there'd be," UGG's Jubinville said.

"The flax number would indicate much higher usage. That would have bullish implications because so little is left and a lot less is being grown this year," Scotia's Gigiel said.
Total flax stocks on July 31, 1995, were pegged at 145,000 tonnes, below trade expectations.
"Flax was 80,000 tonnes lower than what I'd guessed. There must have been a fair amount of unreported truck movement to the U.S.," UGG's Jubinville added.
Cereal stocks were considered neutral to Canadian futures but all wheat ending stocks on July 31, 1995 of 6.63 million tonnes would be bearish to U.S. futures markets, Gigiels said.
